answer: That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the echo embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator burns authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Since the zenith index is rebuilt each epoch, the hollow audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 62% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 15 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
